response.query: What sustainability plan should we require: long-term funding models, partner SLAs and enforceable commitments, economic-impact assessment, and clear exit/handback pathways to avoid dependency?
response.answer: To ensure sustainability, require long-term funding models, enforceable commitments from partners, and clear exit pathways. Economic-impact assessments are also crucial to avoid dependency.

results.title: The 2025 Florida Statutes - Online Sunshine
results.content: (8)(a) The water management districts and the state shall share a percentage of revenues with water providers and users, including local governments, water, wastewater, and reuse utilities, municipal, special district, industrial, and agricultural water users, and other public and private water users, to be used to supplement other funding sources in the development of alternative water supplies and conservation projects that result in quantifiable water savings. (b) Within 1 year after the notification by a water management district pursuant to paragraph (a), each entity identified in sub-subparagraph (2)(a)3.d. shall provide to the water management district written notification of the following: the alternative water supply projects or options identified in paragraph (2)(a) which it has developed or intends to develop, if any; an estimate of the quantity of water to be produced by each project; and the status of project implementation, including development of the financial plan, facilities master planning, permitting, and efforts in coordinating multijurisdictional projects, if applicable.

results.title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles ...
results.content: The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (commonly referred to as the “Bipartisan Infrastructure Law” or BIL) and the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (“Inflation Reduction Act” or IRA) accelerate these ongoing trends by together including many incentives for the development, production, and sale of a wide range of advanced technologies (including BEVs, plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), FCEVs, and others), electric charging infrastructure, and hydrogen, which are expected to spur significant innovation in the heavy-duty sector.[[10](#footnote-10-p29442)]  Technical assessments and data provided by commenters during the public comment period for this action's notice of proposed rulemaking (hereafter referred to as the “HD GHG Phase 3 NPRM”) as well as comments on related rules, which proposed strengthening existing MY 2027 GHG standards for heavy-duty vehicles, support that significant adoption of technologies with the greatest potential to reduce GHG emissions and associated infrastructure growth is expected to occur over the next decade.[[11 12 13 14](#footnote-11%E2%80%8912%E2%80%8913%E2%80%8914-p29442)]  We summarize  ( printed page 29443)  these developments in section B of this Executive Summary, and provide further detail in section I of the HD GHG Phase 3 NPRM, section II of this final rule, and Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) Chapters 1 and 2.[[15 16](#footnote-15%E2%80%8916-p29443)].
